A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MeteoRA with the same authors, base models and core experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and sufficiently complete for comparison.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices A.2–A.3 report original evaluations on 28 individual tasks and composite tasks, including numerical comparisons and an adapter-routing example.

after.justification: Section 4 and the appendices retain original task evaluations and add baseline comparisons, reduced-data experiments and runtime/memory measurements.

M1.justification: v1 Section 3.3 describes contiguous adapter storage and loop-based computation. v3 introduces parallel bmm-torch computation and a fused bmm-triton kernel with blocking, masking and delayed column summation (Appendix A.2, Algorithm 1). These substantially extend the forward procedure; the core routing architecture, frozen adapters and training objectives remain.

E1.justification: The 28 individual tasks and composite-3/5/10 coverage are retained. v3 Section 6 additionally reports testing foreign-language GSM8K problems, with Italian as the example, to investigate combining mathematics and translation knowledge. This is a limited extension of task requirements.

E2.justification: The individual-task comparisons expand from PEFT, LoRA-F and LoRA-B to include Avg Merge, TIES, DARE, Arrow and LoRAHub (v3 Table 1 and Appendix A.4). v3 also introduces single-lora and loop-based efficiency controls, including loop-speedup in Appendix A.7. These are evaluated comparisons, beyond citations already present in v1.

E3.justification: v3 adds 100- and 5-example gate-training conditions, efficiency testing on batch_size × 10 samples per task, and synthetic sweeps over sequence length, batch size, top-k, adapter count and generation length. Runtime, memory and combined cost metrics expand the evaluation protocol. The original 900/100 per-task split and two-shot composite evaluation are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained top-1/top-2 comparisons and routing example, v3 adds reduced-training-data sensitivity tests and extensive efficiency scaling analyses. Section 6 also reports qualitative tests of adapter replacement with versus without gate retraining, and whether combining translation and mathematics adapters improves foreign-language mathematics.

E5.justification: Neither version specifies repeated-run counts, seeds or confidence-interval procedures. v3's new efficiency plots contain shaded bands around some curves, particularly in Figure 7, but their meaning and estimator are undocumented. Whether these constitute newly reported statistical uncertainty cannot be established reliably.

E6.justification: v3 adds extensive baseline, reduced-data and efficiency results. Existing values also change: LlaMA2 PEFT topical_chat BLEU changes from 35.60 in v1 Table 7 to 12.50 in v3 Table 6. Many top-1/top-2 entries exchange assignments without explanation, so they cannot establish performance gains. Composite scores remain identical in the corresponding main and appendix tables.

T1.justification: v3 Appendix A.2 adds an algebraic derivation of blocked multiplication and mask/column-sum reconstruction, including Equation 7. Appendix A.1 revises the token-loss gradient description from affecting the remaining k−1 adapters to all k selected adapters. v1's rough forward-complexity statement disappears; the central routing and loss equations otherwise remain equivalent.

C1.justification: v3 elevates novel GPU forward acceleration and an approximately 4× speedup into the abstract and contribution list; v1 referred generally to an efficient operator. Autonomous selection and composite solving remain central, while v3 Section 4.3 explicitly limits successful composite evaluation to LlaMA3-8B, qualifying v1's abstract claim about both base models.

C2.justification: The new limitations section explains why adapter updates require gate retraining, discusses the lack of improvement from combining adapters for foreign-language GSM8K, and hypothesizes that existing base-model language knowledge makes the translation adapter unnecessary. It also acknowledges residual inference overhead and memory tradeoffs. These substantive applicability boundaries were absent from v1.

D1.justification: v3 adds Triton kernel pseudocode and memory-operation details, gate-training time and Accelerate information, and access links for trained models. It also specifies composite-task temperatures of 15/20/30, a 4,096-token cutoff and 13 skipped samples. These composite settings are newly documented alongside unchanged scores; the PDFs do not establish an experimental rerun.

R1.justification: v3 adds a specific comparison with MixLoRA and references supporting Arrow, DARE, GPU kernels and calibration. The introduction also softens the assertion that existing approaches lack dynamic switching to a lack of supporting evidence. The related-work taxonomy and most existing research positioning remain intact.

P1.justification: The abstract and substantial introduction and method passages are rewritten, background subsections become compact inline topics, and repeated routing discussion is removed. Top-k explanations, dataset splits and composite-evaluation details move into reorganized appendices. Terminology changes throughout, and the broken limitations reference is replaced by an actual section.

P2.justification: v3 adds efficiency Figures 5–8, merges the two model-summary tables, and substantially expands appendix comparison tables. Figure 3 replaces numbered task axes with abbreviations and includes more comparators; Figure 2 adds training/freezing annotations. Figure 4 redisplays the retained example with weight-dependent shading and an additional legend category.

improvement.justification: v1 lacked evaluated adapter-fusion competitors and runtime/memory evidence for its acceleration claims. v3 addresses these important gaps with five additional fusion baselines, specified parallel kernels and efficiency studies, supported by useful reproducibility details and substantive limitations. Reporting inconsistencies remain material: top-1/top-2 assignments change without explanation, and Avg Merge accuracy is 0.370 in Table 1 versus 0.357 in Appendix Table 4. These weaken fine-grained comparisons, but the substantial gains in methodological specification and empirical validation support an overall improvement.
